messages:
maria: seeing a wave of ena interface flaps on c7gn nodes in us-west-2 since ~01:06 UTC, pods reporting network errors and kube-proxy restarts. example from dmesg: 'ena 0000:af:00.0: ENA HW reset detected, link down'
sam: any deploys or firmware changes before that window?
maria: we rolled a kernel + ena driver package at 00:45 for a perf canary. also seeing RX errors and skb allocation failures in kernel logs
cheng: we did a driver bump in the canary earlier (ena 2.1.4 -> 2.1.6). pulling ethtool stats now
maria: ethtool -S ena0 shows: rx_errors:1834 tx_errors:12 rx_no_buf:720 rx_packets:452312 tx_packets:221904
leo: what's MTU/irq setup? many of these symptoms correlate with jumbo MTU + driver bug. try setting MTU to 1500 on a single node as quick mitigation
maria: MTU is 9000 currently, irqbalance is on. lowering MTU on one node now: `sudo ip link set dev ena0 mtu 1500` — will observe
ops-oncall: draining affected nodes and shifting workloads. if not stable within 30m we declare incident and escalate :rotating_light:
infra-bot: [ALERT] net.iface.flap detected on c7gn-pool-usw2 (link down count=52) — https://monitoring.internal/alerts/INC-12345
sam: good call on draining. if MTU rollback doesn't help we should revert the driver package to 2.1.4. Cheng, can you stage a rollback plan?
cheng: got it. prepping rollback bundle and will run a staged rollback across AZs starting with the canary. ETA 45m for canary rollback window
maria: update: MTU change on test node removed rx_no_buf and link hasn't flapped for 12m. keeping MTU at 1500 on test node while we plan next steps
leo: note that we don't use RDMA on this fleet, but path-MTU/fragmentation issues still produce similar RX framing errors at the NIC level
ops-oncall: documenting timeline and tagging this thread for postmortem. moving affected nodes to maintenance until rollback or driver fix confirmed
maria: uploaded condensed logs and ethtool dumps to the incident thread #incidents/inc-2025-07-c7gn-ena
sam: thanks all. keep updates tight here — if we see a spike after rollback testing, ping the pager immediately
